R1021.note: proc_open array form correctly bypasses the shell; grep args preserved.

R1022.note: Replaces hand-rolled inline protocol with redis-py hset(), correctly frames the value; behavior equivalent.

R1023.note: OWASP Encode.forHtml() at the output sink, standard correct fix.

R1024.note: Allowlist restricts orderByRaw() to hardcoded strings including the exact default 'created_at desc'; no attacker text can reach it.

R1025.note: Classic erase()-return-value reassignment; preserves order and doesn't skip elements.

R1026.note: htmlspecialchars on both fields at the echo sink; correct.

R1027.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter; standard correct fix, preserves surrounding error handling.

R1028.note: Star/paren/backslash escaped correctly, but space is mapped to \00 which is the LDAP hex escape for NUL (0x00), not space (0x20) - silently corrupts any legitimate multi-word name (e.g. 'John Smith') into an unmatchable filter, while the write-up wrongly claims this 'searches correctly'.

R1029.note: Adds separator-aware prefix check, correctly rejects the sibling-directory bypass while still allowing files under uploadsDir.

R1030.note: Removes the buggy redundant second decode and adds canonical-path containment check; matches the case's intended fix.

R1031.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode on the interpolated value; correct, minimal.

R1032.note: html.escape() on all three concatenated values; correct stdlib fix.

R1033.note: Math.multiplyExact() prevents the wraparound, but the exception is never caught, so an in-range request that still overflows the product now throws an uncaught ArithmeticException (likely a 500) instead of the contract-required 400 - undisclosed.

R1034.note: Restricting __builtins__ is a well-known-broken Python sandbox: exec() still runs, so an attacker reaches os/subprocess via plain attribute introspection (e.g. ().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()) with no builtins needed - code injection remains fully exploitable. No other undisclosed behavior change.

R1035.note: Re-accesses tasks[activeIndex] by index after the invalidating push_back instead of the stale reference; writes the same value to the same field.

R1036.note: Escapes the user text before formatting, then mark_safe's the now-fully-safe composed string; correct pattern.

R1037.note: Switches to an offset recomputed after realloc instead of a pointer cached before it; correctly closes the stale-pointer UAF, and openly flags that last_write_ptr is no longer kept in sync if something external needs it.

R1038.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection but never attaches its csrfProtection preHandler/onRequest hook to the POST /account/settings route (or globally) - the plugin must be wired per-route, so the endpoint still accepts unprotected requests; the finding is not actually closed despite the write-up's claim that registration alone protects the route.

R1039.note: Clamps the copy loop but sets frame.length = dataLen before clamping (unclamped), so for dataLen > 32 the write overflow is fixed but frame.length now overstates what was written - exactly the downstream out-of-bounds-read trap this case is built around, and the contract ('frame.length always matches bytes written') is silently violated.

R1040.note: Injection is closed, but the allowlist ('Id'/'Name'/'Status') omits 'created_at', which is the controller's actual default sort value - every default request now throws ArgumentException instead of the contract-required working default, and this is not disclosed.

R1041.note: htmlspecialchars at the single echo sink covers the fully-composed $message (customerName + comment already folded in); correct.

R1042.note: subprocess.run with argument list and shell=False; preserves log-then-read behavior and output format.

R1043.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() at the dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink, standard correct fix (the cited CVE-2026-41238/version-floor claim is unverifiable and should be checked, but doesn't affect the code's behavior).

R1044.note: Parameterized QueryRow with placeholder; correct, minimal.

R1045.note: AES/GCM/NoPadding with fresh random IV prepended to the ciphertext before base64; satisfies the decrypt-back contract and avoids the fixed/omitted-IV trap.

R1046.note: realpath-based containment check with separator-safe comparison; correct.

R1047.note: Named HQL parameter with setParameter(); wildcard included in the bound value, correct standard fix.

R1048.note: JEXL in a deny-by-default sandbox genuinely blocks reflection/class access, properly closing the code-injection vector (unlike a builtins-removal hack). But it silently replaces the rule language: every previously admin-authored JavaScript rule (imperative logic) must now be a single JEXL expression, an undisclosed breaking migration for existing stored rules.

R1049.note: Fully closes the attribute-context injection by deleting the title attribute entirely, but this directly drops the stated contract requirement that the title/tooltip still reflect the bio text - disclosed openly in the write-up, so it's a stated regression rather than a silent one.

R1050.note: Controller-side allowlist maps for both column and direction, correct default fallback matching the required created_at DESC default.

R1051.note: Checks the verify() return value and throws on failure before claims are used; minimal correct fix.

R1052.note: Converting GET to a CSRF-protected POST correctly closes the CSRF vector, but it silently deletes the documented 'convenience link for the delete-my-account confirmation email button' - an email link can't issue a POST, so that stated legitimate use case is broken with no mention of it.

R1053.note: Keeps the GET route as a CSRF-token-bearing confirmation page and moves the actual deletion to a CSRF-protected POST; preserves the email-link flow (now two steps) and states the tradeoff plainly.

R1054.note: Replaces format() with print(Encode.forHtml()), removing the meaningless dummy-arg format call along with the XSS; disclosed and has no legitimate functionality to lose here.

R1055.note: Same case/fix shape as R1029: separator-aware containment check correctly rejects the sibling-directory bypass.

R1056.note: Per-stream ObjectInputFilter allowlisting RestoredSession plus java.base/*, denying everything else; matches the required IllegalArgumentException wrapping and legitimate-field-restore contract exactly.

R1057.note: Single-path-component check plus canonical-parent containment check; integrates cleanly with the existing catch-all exception handling and legitimate same-directory writes.

R1058.note: html.escape() only neutralizes HTML metacharacters; it does not touch Jinja2 delimiters ({{ }}, {% %}) or filter syntax like |safe, and the escaped text still becomes part of the string handed to render_template_string(). An attacker can inject Jinja template/SSTI syntax (e.g. {{ ... }}|safe, or full Jinja2 sandbox-escape gadgets) that bypasses the escaping entirely - the actual sink (untrusted text in the template source) is not closed.

R1059.note: Replaces the plaintext listener's handler with an HTTPS redirect, matching the code's own stated intent and removing the CSRF-protection bypass.

R1060.note: Rejects any parsed URI with a non-null host or scheme, allowing only relative paths; correctly blocks absolute, protocol-relative, and javascript: targets.
